headline: Mandatory Registration and Polar Bear Safety Orientations
reservation: All visitors must register with Parks Canada and attend a mandatory safety and orientation briefing in Pond Inlet or Arctic Bay before entry. Independent travelers require specialized permits, and those using local outfitters should confirm their guide's current licensing and park authorization.

days.title: Bylot Island Glaciers and Bird Cliffs
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Pond Inlet via boat

stops.name: Aktineq Glacier
stops.detail: Observe the massive ice flow descending from the mountains toward the sea, typical of the park's High Arctic landscape.

stops.name: Bylot Island Migratory Bird Sanctuary
stops.detail: View the sheer cliffs of Cape Graham Moore where thousands of Thick-billed Murres nest during the brief summer window.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 4 hours for boat transfer across Eclipse Sound; sea conditions are highly variable.
days.note: Travel is entirely dependent on ice breakup and sea states; daily plans may be delayed by local weather.

days.title: Oliver Sound Fjords

stops.name: Oliver Sound
stops.detail: Navigate the long, narrow fjord flanked by steep granite walls and hanging glaciers for a classic Arctic waterway experience.

stops.name: Borden Peninsula Coastline
stops.detail: Explore the hoodoos and unique geological erosions found along the coastal fringes of the peninsula.

days.driving: Logistics are managed via local charter; travel times vary significantly based on engine type and ice floes.
days.note: This is a remote wilderness area with no developed facilities; self-sufficiency is required for all landings.

days.title: Tuniit Ruins and Arctic Tundra
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Nuvut Point vicinity

stops.name: Nuvut Point
stops.detail: Examine the archaeological sites of the Tuniit (Dorset) and Thule cultures that once inhabited these shores.

stops.name: Lowland Tundra Valleys
stops.detail: Walk the spongy tundra to see Arctic poppies and dwarf willows while scanning for caribou or Arctic fox.

days.driving: Local walking or boat shuttle; no road access exists between sites.
days.note: Strict regulations govern the proximity to archaeological sites; do not disturb any artifacts or stones.

intel.title: Logistics Hubs
intel.text: There are no parking lots in the park; all logistics occur at the shoreline in Pond Inlet or Arctic Bay. Vehicles are limited to ATVs or snowmobiles within the gateway communities.

intel.title: Emergency Communication
intel.text: No cellular service exists within the park boundaries. Visitors must carry a satellite communication device or an EPIRB and know how to operate it in High Arctic latitudes.

intel.title: Community Supply Only
intel.text: Fuel is available only in the gateway hamlets; check with local outfitters for fuel drums required for long-distance boat charters. There are no resupply points once you depart the community.

intel.title: The Midnight Sun
intel.text: During July and August, 24-hour daylight is present, which can disrupt sleep patterns. The 'summer' window is extremely short, usually limited to these two months for water access.

intel.title: Ice-Dependent Movement
intel.text: Entry is generally by boat in summer or snowmobile in winter; there are no roads into the park. Access is strictly governed by ice freeze-up and break-up cycles which vary annually.

plan.arrival: Fly into Pond Inlet or Arctic Bay; report immediately to the Parks Canada office for your scheduled orientation and permit validation.
plan.vehicle: No cars or RVs; all transport is via chartered boat, aircraft, or local outfitter equipment.
plan.goldenHour: The 'Midnight Sun' provides continuous light, but low-angle sun over the Aktineq Glacier in late August creates deep textures on the ice.
